title: Double O Twins
kidRule: Two O's together usually say a long 'oo' as in cartoon or a short, quick 'oo' as in wooden, and both sounds are spelled the same way. (Blood and flood are famous rule-breakers!)
hint: Listen for the vowel sound that a pair of twin letters makes. It can be long or short and quick, but the same twins make both. Which twins are they?
reminder: Whether the sound is long or short, it is spelled with twin O's: O-O.

check.question: Why does CARTOON have two O's near the end?
check.correctAnswer: Two O's team up to make the 'oo' sound!
distractors: Because cartoons are drawn with lots of round circles
Because one O is silent and the other does the talking

words.def: A funny drawing, or a show made of drawings that seem to move.
words.sent: We watched a cartoon about a dancing robot.
words.story: To make an old hand-drawn cartoon, artists had to draw as many as 24 pictures for every single second of film!
words.card: A *car* in my favorite *cartoon* honks in burps!

words.def: Made from the hard part of a tree.
words.sent: Grandpa carved a wooden spoon for stirring soup.
words.story: A temple in Japan called Horyuji has wooden buildings that are about 1,300 years old, the oldest in the world!
words.card: The *wood* pile dreamed of becoming a *wooden* pirate ship!

words.def: A thin rubber bag that gets big when you fill it with air.
words.sent: My red balloon floated up to the ceiling.
words.story: The first rubber balloon was made in 1824 by a scientist named Michael Faraday!
words.card: My *balloon* thinks it is a *ball* and keeps bouncing on the ceiling!

words.sent: Once the teacher drew a picture, I understood the puzzle.
words.story: A border collie named Chaser understood the names of more than 1,000 different toys!
words.card: The dog *stood* on his head until everyone *understood* that he wanted a treat!

words.def: A bird that taps on tree trunks with its strong beak to find insects.
words.sent: A woodpecker was drumming on the old oak tree.
words.story: A woodpecker can peck up to 20 times in one second, and its long tongue wraps around the inside of its skull!
words.card: The *woodpecker* gave the tree one tiny *peck* and said, 'Knock knock!'

words.def: A furry animal with a black mask on its face and a striped, bushy tail.
words.sent: A raccoon tipped over our trash can last night.
words.story: Raccoons have very sensitive front paws, and they often feel their food underwater before eating it!
words.card: The *raccoon* likes to *coo* like a dove while it borrows your snacks!

words.def: The silky case a caterpillar spins around itself while it changes into a moth.
words.sent: The moth wriggled out of its cocoon.
words.story: Silk comes from silkworm cocoons, and one cocoon is made of a single thread that can be more than half a mile long!
words.card: My *co*zy caterpillar ordered a pizza to her *cocoon*!

words.def: A big Australian animal that hops on strong back legs and carries its baby in a pouch.
words.sent: The kangaroo hopped across the dusty plain.
words.story: A baby kangaroo is called a joey, and when it is born it is only about the size of a jelly bean!
words.card: The *kangaroo* kept a b*roo*m in her pouch to sweep the desert!

words.def: A curved throwing stick that can fly in a circle and come back to you.
words.sent: He threw the boomerang and it curved back toward him.
words.story: Boomerangs were invented by the first peoples of Australia thousands of years ago, and many kinds were made for hunting and did not come back at all!
words.card: *Boo*! My *boomerang* came back wearing a ghost costume!

words.def: The area around your home and the people who live there.
words.sent: Everyone in our neighborhood came to the block party.
words.story: In Britain this word is spelled with an extra letter U, right after the first O!
words.card: Every horse in my *neighborhood* wears a fuzzy *hood* in winter!
